newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds end weaker, underperform U.S. market.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds end weaker, underperform U.S. market.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed weaker on Thursday, underperforming their U.S. counterparts, amid some profit taking on recent spead narrowing and disappointment the Bank of Canada did not cut rates, dealers said.

"I think it was just a consolidation move in the market. I didn't see anything fundamental that should trigger this," said Arve Bendiksrud, fixed-income analyst with TD Securities. "It's come a very long way in a very short time."
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond fell C$0.95 to C$109.90 to yield 7.161 percent. The U.S. 30-year benchmark fell 9/32 to yield 6.85 percent.
The spread between the benchmark bonds widened to 31 basis points from 25 basis points at the close of trading on Wednesday.
Canadian long bonds have sharply outperformed their U.S. counterparts this week, with spreads reaching their lowest levels since 1985 on Tuesday.

Weaker than expected economic data earlier this week and recent strength in the Canadian dollar also bolstered expectations that the Bank of Canada would cut interest rates this morning. The failure of the bank to cut rates helped weaken short-term bonds, analysts said.
"People weren't really sure why it didn't happen, because it seemed to have all the makings of a rate cut based on the conditions that existed when they cut last time," said Bendiksrud.
A drop in U.S. Treasuries also helped weaken Canadian bonds, analysts said. The U.S. market tumbled this morning after the release of lower-than-expected jobless claims for the week ended October 19.
In other prices, the Government of Canada 7.0 percent of 2006 fell C$0.85 to C$103.25 to yield 6.554 percent. The U.S. 10-year benchmark fell 5/32 to yield 6.57 percent.
The negative spread between the 10-year bonds narrowed to 2 basis points, from 12 basis points at Wednesday's close.
The three-month cash bill traded at 3.23 percent against the U.S. three-month bill at 5.12 percent.
